title: Insurance agent
tagline: Learn to guide families through protection planning with clarity and care.
setting: Conversations happen in home offices, kitchen tables, and video calls where families make long-term financial decisions.

scenarios.label: First kitchen table meeting
scenarios.desc: A young couple reviews their finances after buying a house and agrees to hear options.
scenarios.setup: You sit at their kitchen table with a laptop open. The husband says, ‘We just closed on the house, so money is tight, but we know we need something.’
scenarios.objective: Uncover their top three worries and agree on a follow-up with quotes.

scenarios.label: Term vs whole life comparison
scenarios.desc: A single parent weighs term affordability against whole life cash value for a child’s future.
scenarios.setup: You share a screen on a video call. The prospect leans forward and says, ‘Show me the numbers side by side so I can see what I’m actually paying for.’
scenarios.objective: Present a clear comparison and secure a preference for one structure.

scenarios.label: Bundling home and life at renewal
scenarios.desc: A longtime homeowner resists adding life coverage at renewal, citing cost and complexity.
scenarios.setup: You stand at their counter with the renewal packet. The homeowner taps the page and says, ‘My premium already jumped fifteen percent. Why would I add more now?’
scenarios.objective: Reframe the bundle as a discount and protection upgrade, then ask for the application.
scenarios.moment: Saturday 10:30 am, dust motes in sunbeams

buyers.angle: They track every dollar and need proof that coverage fits their tight cash flow.
She wants the conversation efficient and hates jargon.
She will compare every decimal point and needs the child rider explained simply.
He has read Reddit threads and challenges every assumption with spreadsheets.

buyers.personality: loyal to current carrier, price-sensitive, blunt
buyers.angle: He sees the bundle as an upsell and trusts his agent of twenty years over new math.

objections: Term is cheap enough, why pay triple for whole life?
I can invest the difference myself and do better
My employer gives me life insurance already
The house is insured, that’s the big asset
I’ll wait until the kids are older
Your competitor quoted twenty percent less
I don’t trust insurance companies to pay out
The medical exam is a hassle I don’t have time for

rubric.label: Needs discovery
rubric.what: Asks open questions that reveal family priorities, debts, and fears before quoting.

rubric.label: Plain explanation
rubric.what: Translates riders, exclusions, and cash value into everyday language without jargon.

rubric.label: Budget framing
rubric.what: Positions premiums as a percentage of income and shows trade-offs the prospect accepts.

rubric.label: Objection handling
rubric.what: Acknowledges the concern, reframes with a concrete example, and checks for agreement.

rubric.label: Compliance honesty
rubric.what: Discloses limitations, waiting periods, and suitability rules even when it slows the sale.

rubric.label: Close clarity
rubric.what: Summarises the exact next step, documents required, and timeline in one sentence.

pitfalls: Illustrating non-guaranteed cash values as promises.
Skipping the suitability questionnaire to speed the application.
Bundling without showing the standalone home premium for comparison.
line: Selling life and home insurance to individuals and families

personas.name: Nolan Bredesen
personas.background: They are buying their first house with a modest down payment and are watching every expense. Their savings are tied up in the purchase so they need insurance that won’t strain their cash flow.
pushbacks: I can invest the difference myself and do better
My employer gives me life insurance already
I’ll wait until the kids are older

clear proof of value over cost
no hidden fees or surprise charges
